content.comment_body: Hello, I am having trouble with my ethernet card not being recognized by [product_name]. I have tried several solutions recommended by [company_name] (such as running as administrator and reinstalling the ethernet driver). The card works on other laptops, but it isn't detected by any laptop at my workplace. My [product_name] version is [version_no]. Are there any suggestions or solutions for this issue? Thanks.
Are the drivers for your ethernet network adapter current? Does the name of the ethernet adapter include any special characters?
Yes, the drivers are updated. Here is an image of my ethernet adapter.
This relates to my ethernet adapter.

I notice there is a special character (#) in the network adapter's name. I'm not sure exactly which special characters are restricted, but perhaps this could be a factor. Previous versions of [product_name] had issues when the adapter name included special characters.
How can I remove or modify it?
I'm not sure, as I'm not an IT expert.
I have another question: Can you use this network adapter to access the internet? Your previous screenshot appears to show a problem with the ethernet connection.
I can access the internet using both WiFi and an ethernet cable.
Does [product_name] display the WiFi adapter in the connection window?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering issues with [product_name] failing to detect certain ethernet adapters, even though the hardware operates on other devices and drivers are up to date. The issue may be related to special characters present in the adapter name, which have reportedly caused problems in earlier [product_name] versions. There are uncertainties surrounding how to address adapter name constraints and a lack of detailed information about accepted naming conventions.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects [product_name] software to consistently identify and connect to all functional ethernet adapters on the operating system, regardless of network adapter naming formats.
